briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: DEA Says Marijuana 'Can No Longer Remain in Schedule I' — While Michigan Operators Fight, Adapt, and Keep Opening
briefs.top: Federal momentum is real: the DEA itself has now told its judge that cannabis no longer meets Schedule I criteria, putting a rescheduling recommendation on the near horizon alongside a fast-moving FDA psychedelics pipeline. In Michigan, the 24% wholesale tax fight heads to trial this month, but new stores, court wins, and hospitality-forward formats show operators finding real paths forward.

local.text: Ann Arbor-based C3 Industries opened its Black-owned, women-led High Profile Cannabis Shop on Detroit's east side, the company's first Detroit location and a milestone for the city's social equity licensing program.

Jars Cannabis notched a rare enforcement win, negotiating removal of a Madison Heights surveillance camera trained on its parking lot after the city had threatened punishment over a blocked sightline.

Muskegon's Fields Cannary is pushing the retail format forward with a hospitality-first dispensary-and-restaurant buildout targeting a fall opening, a bet that experience-driven concepts can outrun tax-driven margin pressure.

Rize, which runs three Upper Michigan stores, is proving the tax survivable by negotiating cost-sharing deals with suppliers to split the 24% wholesale burden rather than eating it alone — a playbook other operators are watching.

The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's first lawsuit against the 24% wholesale tax is finally headed to trial this month, giving operators a real courtroom shot at relief even as a second unconstitutionality suit over 'tax pyramiding' proceeds and a GOP-backed repeal bill (HB 6224) sits in the Legislature.

national.text: The DEA made its strongest statement yet for reform, telling the administrative law judge in its final post-hearing brief that marijuana 'can no longer remain in Schedule I,' a striking reversal from the agency that has long led federal enforcement against cannabis.

With closing arguments filed and the corrected hearing transcript now public, Chief ALJ Derek Julius is set to issue his Schedule III recommendation to the DEA Administrator — the next real milestone toward federal rescheduling.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy COMP360 keeps clearing hurdles: after two positive Phase 3 trials, the FDA granted a rolling NDA review and a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher that could shrink review time to just 1-2 months, positioning it to be the first approved psilocybin medicine.

Cannabis consolidation is accelerating at the top: Curaleaf's roughly $1.5 billion-plus cross-border takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis and Vireo Growth's $49 million PharmaCann Colorado buy plus its pending Planet 13 merger signal multistate operators are betting big on scale ahead of federal reform.

The FDA is building out formal psychedelics infrastructure, finalizing its clinical-trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and scheduling a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic use — moves analysts say create 'a more supportive regulatory environment' for developers like Compass, Atai, Cybin and GH Research.
